topic: Whether OPP-019 merits a deep dive as a confidence-aware cardiac procedure-planning opportunity
hypothesis: A reliability envelope over plausible image and model variations could make patient-specific VT and CRT planning outputs safer to interpret; some foundational image-quality, anatomy, registration, and provenance components may be reusable, while indication-specific decision modules remain separate.

arguments.argument: The two JHTV records describe different workflows: CT+BSPM for CRT implantation planning and CT/inFAT-based personalized modeling for VT ablation. The VT record reports retrospective validation but also says further development is needed. Independent 2026 work supports examining uncertainty in CT-derived VT models; it does not validate these JHTV assets.

JHTV technology 24301: CT and body-surface-potential-mapping CRT planning toolbox
JHTV technology 42306: Personalized Heart Modeling Using Intramyocardial Fat Deposition on CT

arguments.argument: A clear reliability display may feel safer and more trustworthy to clinicians; it may also feel distracting or create false reassurance. This is an unmeasured user-reaction hypothesis, not an interview finding.

The strongest risk is that uncertainty is poorly calibrated or the two procedures require incompatible data and models. External CT research shows that small scar-reconstruction changes can alter VT predictions; CT+BSPM CRT planning has different inputs and endpoints. A shared product could add cost without enough shared infrastructure.

arguments.argument: If a reliability envelope identifies unstable predictions and helps clinicians decide when to trust, review, or abstain from a model output, it could improve the usefulness of both planning workflows. The JHU MRI-based feasibility report makes patient-specific model-guided VT planning a credible area to investigate, but does not demonstrate value for the JHTV CT technologies or a shared platform.

arguments.argument: Test a confidence-aware layer first on the VT module, where 2026 CT literature directly documents reconstruction sensitivity; then test the CRT module separately. Share only proven foundations such as image-quality checks, coordinates, provenance and review UI. If reuse is weak, keep two products and test the reliability layer on the stronger single indication.

arguments.argument: Next: agree on clinically meaningful stability and abstention criteria before outcome review; run an exploratory, blinded retrospective feasibility study on separate VT and CRT cohorts; record image exclusions, output stability, clinician review, analyst time and runtime. Treat this as a protocol proposal, not a clinical recommendation or powered efficacy study.
